summary.headline: RACL Geartech FY26 consolidated revenue rose over 20% to ₹512 crore, with Q4 revenue up ~48% YoY to ₹136.69 crore and FY27 guidance of ₹565 crore ±5%.
summary.overview: Management reported all-time high FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹512.42 crore (up from ₹425 crore) and consolidated EBITDA of ₹229.16 crore at 25.21% margin. Q4 consolidated revenue was ₹136.69 crore (up ~48% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 24.93% and PBT of ₹16.91 crore. Debt fell to ₹221 crore from ₹297 crore after equity infusion, and debt-equity improved to 0.63x from 1.3x. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of ₹565 crore ±5% and a ₹1,000 crore revenue ambition in roughly 3 to 5 years, with a stated aim of reaching it by FY29 if possible.

financial_highlights.change: vs ~₹297 crore FY25; debt-equity 0.63x vs 1.3x; current ratio 1.38x vs 1.05x

segments.name: Vehicle segments (% of FY26 turnover)
segments.commentary: Commercial vehicles ~20%, recreational vehicles ~18%, passenger cars ~13% (nil in FY23), tractor/agriculture ~10%, two-wheelers ~30% (down from 40-45%).

segments.name: Geography (FY26)
segments.commentary: Exports ~75% of turnover (Europe ~69%, Asia Pacific and India ~29%, US and Canada ~2%); export turnover ₹346.68 crore consolidated, domestic ₹110 crore.

segments.name: Royal Enfield
segments.commentary: High-volume 350cc five-speed gearbox gears from Gajraula; commercial production expected August-September 2026. Current RE volume about 10,000 motorcycles, targeted to double to 20,000 over time.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹565 crore ±5%; management said it is not revising guidance as the ±5% band is intentional flexibility.
Budgeted FY27 capex ₹77.45 crore, to be funded partly by new bank debt.
Vision of ₹1,000 crore revenue in roughly 3 to 5 years; CEO indicated a wish to reach it by FY29 but said it will not be rushed.
Management said growth beyond ~20% is constrained by capital intensity, plant lead times and team capacity; it prefers sustainable growth.
Titan (BMW EV) mass production targeted October 2026; Venus (BMW EV sports car) October-November 2026, after August sign-off.
Kawasaki: 15 parts, nine pilot lots; SOP targeted October 2026 with mass production from January 2027.
capex_capacity: Budgeted FY27 capex of ₹77.45 crore, with corresponding bank debt to be availed.
Project Crystal (electric power steering for US market with ZF Rane): 600-set sampling under validation in Mexico and US; large capacity build-out and capex planned next year.
Shift drum project: SOP next month, ~150,000 units per annum, with six to seven part numbers to follow over the next year.
Two plants: Gajraula (main) and Noida; Austrian subsidiary and European warehouses.
Royal Enfield supply chain investments lined up in the last quarter; new engine gear business can start by August 2026 subject to supplier finalisation.
demand_pricing: Management said there has been no slowdown in European OEM orders so far; demand described as robust.
Commercial vehicle growth in FY26 came from existing customers (MAN) as the four-year resourcing roadmap completed in 2025; management said future growth will be organic.
Input cost inflation is high; management is negotiating interim cost support with customers, and a weaker rupee partly offsets it.
Raw materials are largely domestic; imports are about 2-5% of raw materials (bearings, oil seals, bought-out parts).
Kawasaki and Royal Enfield new projects expected to add volume; management said the value per kit for RE is not public.
BHEL empanelment received; supplies have started to approved vendor list; ZF orders recovering after weak FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is per-kit value and TAM for the Royal Enfield business; is there scope to move from gears to assemblies?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-kit value not disclosed. Assemblies not currently demanded by RE, though RACL supplies full gearboxes to TVS and KTM and has the capability.

qa_highlights.question: Why can growth not exceed 20% given recovery from Europe and KTM issues?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20% on ₹500 crore adds ₹100 crore in absolute terms; growth is constrained by capital intensity, lead times and quality of ramp-up, so it targets sustainable growth.

qa_highlights.question: Capex needed beyond FY27 for a ₹1,000 crore target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex beyond FY27 will be disclosed once documents are ready; Crystal will require significant additional investment.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to US tariffs, European demand slowdown and currency risk?
qa_highlights.answer: US dollar exports are only 2-3%; exports go via EU, Mexico and Canada. No slowdown seen; rupee depreciation helps partly offset inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue from new projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue not disclosed; management said about 10,000-20,000 motorcycles could run on the parts if demand is met.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 gross margin lower and is guidance being revised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some expenses shift between Q3 and Q4; no revision to FY27 guidance, which retains ±5% flexibility.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation (Middle East-related supply issues) and pressure to pass costs to customers.
Dependence on Royal Enfield, BMW EV programmes (Titan and Venus) and Kawasaki ramp-up timelines (SOP October 2026).
Capex needs for Project Crystal and the ₹1,000 crore ambition; debt funding will follow assured business.
Q4 gross margin softness and quarterly expense timing; watch the first carbon disclosure promised from next quarter.
Shift drum and Crystal validations; ZF order recovery after a weak FY26.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on revenue and margin milestones, while cautious on pace: management repeatedly stressed sustainable growth over faster growth and declined to disclose per-kit values, pricing and specific margins by segment.
key_quotes: We have achieved the milestone figure of 500 plus CR.
Our all gross profit, EBITDA, PBT, PAT, everything has grown as compared to last year.
So far we are not witnessing any slowdown. Demand is really robust.
we have guidance of 565 plus minus 5% for FY27 in Q3.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance of ₹565 crore ±5% (about 10-12% over FY26 ₹512 crore) with management also citing ~20% growth per year; backed partly by Royal Enfield gearbox gears, Shift drum SOP (~150,000 units/yr), Kawasaki and Titan/Venus EV SOPs, and robust European demand, but no specific order values or utilisation numbers were given.
